_comment: Public facts about Alexey only. Every item must be publishable: CV/LinkedIn level, no client identities, no psychometrics, no pricing, no holdings, no P&L. Pro bono work is never presented as employment.
name: Alexey Malashonak
summary: Risk, data and product leader with 14+ years in quantitative finance. Nine years at UBS Group Risk Control, ending as Director and Product Owner of the universal semantic data model for 600+ users. Shipped a regulated counterparty-risk product to market in seven months in 2013. Since 2026 builds tested software with AI coding agents under explicit human controls.

timeline.role: AI Engineer & Advisor, Risk and Finance
Career break: relocation Kyiv → Zürich; CFA charter completed 2017

education.note: Highest thesis grade in the programme (42 students defended)

education.where: Kyiv School of Economics / University of Houston

recommendations.quote: Relentless in building things the right way... forward-thinking mindset is rare... solution-oriented.
Extremely sharp. Ability to grasp new concepts and find solutions is truly impressive.

dimensions._comment: The five project characteristics the viewer controls. 0 = left label, 100 = right label.

cases.title: Universal semantic data model, UBS
cases.headline: Built and owned the first universal data model and semantic language for UBS Group Risk Control; it became the most-consumed risk report at UBS.
points: Owned the semantic data model end to end as Product Owner; 600+ users across Switzerland, the US and Singapore.
Architected the Group Risk Control data integration for the UBS–Credit Suisse merger; multiple legacy systems decommissioned.
Chosen as the strategic foundation for the UBS–CS risk reporting integration.

cases.title: Reporting operating model redesign, UBS
cases.headline: Digitalised 95% of legacy regulatory reports in two years and 76% of interactive content in 18 months by redesigning the operating model, not porting reports.
points: Led a team of six engineers as Development Team Lead.
Regulatory and management reporting for FINMA, SNB and overseas regulators across three jurisdictions.
Promoted from Associate Director to Director in under three years.

cases.title: Counterparty credit risk product, PrevioRisk
cases.headline: Delivered a full CCR/CVA risk system to market in seven months against an eleven-month scope, managing 15 developers.
points: Turned legal agreements (ISDA, netting, collateral/CSA terms) into exposure-aggregation product logic.
Basel 2/3/3.5 capital for 1,500+ trades computed in about 7 seconds; OCC/FRS-compliant supervisory reporting.
Validated pricing for 50+ structured product types; owned client communication and quality control.

cases.title: Retail credit risk forecasting, Raiffeisen Bank Aval
cases.headline: Built a forecasting system for a USD 3bn+ retail portfolio (500,000+ loans); monthly risk-cost forecast error around 2.5% over 16 months.
points: Combined flow-rate models, Markov chains, macro models and behavioural scorecards into one system.
Methodology awarded by the regional head of Raiffeisen Group.

cases.title: Distressed portfolio valuation, VostokFinance
cases.headline: Redesigned the pre-deal valuation scorecard: GINI from 0.16 to 0.59, valuation effort from 6 to 0.1 man-hours per case.
points: Built an investment valuation and cash-flow planning system for purchased portfolios.
Reforecasting with segmentation and macro and operational variables.

cases.title: Risk-governed autonomous trading engine
cases.headline: Built an event-driven trading engine (~35k lines, 288 tests) with AI coding agents, where an autonomous strategy can never act outside limits a human set in advance.
points: Two-stage risk layer, independent kill switch drilled live, append-only journal of every decision.
Seven go-live gates written before any engine code; paper trading only, no P&L claimed.
83 commits in under four weeks; ~6,900 lines of design documentation.

cases.title: Typed AI model as a governed research instrument
cases.headline: Used Jev, a structured-output AI model, to score 10,988 news events, and built the controls that decide whether its output can be trusted.
points: Knowledge-cutoff contamination test (4,070 calls) before any scoring; result disclosed as inconclusive.
Pre-registered hypotheses, holdout, multiple-testing ledger; 15 of 19 hypotheses killed by the regime.
Found no directional signal and a clear magnitude signal; reported both plainly.

cases.title: AI CV-review tool for CFA Society Switzerland (pro bono)
cases.headline: Conceived and built an AI CV-review tool that turned a manual member service into a calibrated, auditable workflow, deployed on GitHub Pages.
points: Codified an expert reviewer's heuristics into a 7-dimension rubric; fixed systematic score inflation (~88% vs 58–70% expected).
Pinned model, golden-snapshot drift regression, noise floor from repeat runs, a human gate on every output.
Privacy by default: no server-side storage of candidate data.
proves: AI product from zero to live

cases.title: Auditable analytics engine for finance (own build, method)
cases.headline: Designed and built a six-layer analytics engine that reproduces a published finance figure automatically, as rules at a commit × data at a snapshot hash.
points: Freeze / verify / serve: a reconciliation gate that fails closed; a stale or altered snapshot is refused, never served.
Governed what-if simulators with ranges, sources, thresholds and reverse stress; facts kept separate from scenarios.
108 tests; logic written as SQL so it ports to a production engine.

cases.title: AI-native delivery under human control
cases.headline: Runs day-to-day engineering through a designed system of AI agents: Claude Code as lead engineer, Codex for mechanical tasks, every diff reviewed before merge.
points: Written task briefs, isolated worktrees, acceptance checks run by the lead, not the agent.
Model tiering as a cost and quality decision; pinned versions re-baselined on upgrade.
Human-in-the-loop by construction: no agent sends mail, enters passwords or submits forms.
proves: AI-assisted development as a working method
speed from idea to working product

cases.title: EMBA thesis: decision support for portfolio managers
cases.headline: Built a news-shock indicator (FinBERT NLP + market data) and tested it with 53 professional portfolio managers; highest thesis grade in the programme.
points: Significant association with experts' risk decisions (β = −0.49, p = 0.0015).
Reported the null result on outcomes plainly: an adoption insight for decision-support tools.
~13,400 lines of reproducible Python.

cases.title: Digital presence for a Swiss sports club (pro bono)
cases.headline: Took a non-profit club from zero web presence to an indexed, legally compliant bilingual site at about CHF 12 a year.
points: Rejected CMS and paid hosting deliberately: lowest viable cost for the client's reality.
Domain registered to the club's legal entity; photo consent under Swiss data protection law.

gaps.title: No KYC/AML/KYT product built
gaps.detail: Regulatory work so far is risk, capital and supervisory reporting. Onboarding and transaction-monitoring flows would be new.

gaps.title: No private-markets or tokenisation delivery
gaps.detail: Securities, derivatives and deal-valuation mechanics are covered; syndication, SPV and on-chain settlement experience is not.

gaps.title: Last regulated product shipped to external clients was in 2013
gaps.detail: Since then the regulated work was inside a bank. Recent shipping evidence is own builds, without external regulated clients.

gaps.title: No formal software-engineering background
gaps.detail: No CS degree and no production engineering employment. Builds with AI agents under tests and review; the codebases are evidence, not a job title.

gaps.title: No scaled-fintech product organisation
gaps.detail: Product leadership was inside a bank and a 2013 software firm, not in a payments, banking or spend-management scale-up.
